answer: Shared-fate escrow: each identity’s actions draw from one operator-linked reserve, and a proven sybil cluster forfeits the whole reserve, not just the offending wallet. The kernel of enforcement is cross-identity liability, so an attacker must fund every clone at full reserve value before any one sybil can act. Each fake identity thus costs the operator a real, non-recoverable escrow and the marble of collateral tied to its siblings. A single voyage of fraudulent transactions liquidates that reserve across the cluster.
